text.p: Eurotunnel Plc, the debt-laden Channel Tunnel operator, signalled a possible end to the cross-Channel price war with ferries on Thursday by announcing a hike in the summer season prices for the Le Shuttle service.

The Anglo-French operator said the prices will rise by between 40 and 70 stg above existing prices from March 26 onwards. The economy price for a car and up to six passengers staying away for at least six days will be 169 stg, rising to 199 stg in peak periods. The cost of a mini-break will be 109 stg, with the peak fare at 129 stg.
A Eurotunnel spokeswoman said summer prices tended to be higher than in the winter season.

But analysts have been expecting an end to the escalation of the price war between the cross-Channel ferry companies and Eurotunnel for some time. The policy was seen as unsustainable, with both sides suffering a heavy toll on profitability.

Eurotunnel has already seen its revenues hit by the impact of lost market share following a fire in a main tunnel last November which seriously disrupted services and which will not be fully repaired until the spring.

Bill Dix, managing director of the Le Shuttle service, said in a statement that he was confident the latest tariffs coupled with the policy of offering the lowest duty free prices would appeal to customers as Eurotunnel seeks to regain its market position in the aftermath of the fire.
